themes_detail.label: Tree branches hazard spike
themes_detail.summary: Overgrown tree and branch complaints surged to 3 THIS WEEK versus a 0.4 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 700% spike (z-score: 5.42)—suggesting either a weather event, deferred maintenance, or rapid deterioration affecting multiple blocks in Riverdale/Fieldston.
evidence: 3 overgrown tree/branch complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly baseline (700% increase, z-score: 5.42)
Aligns with community board's repeated budget request for 'new equipment for maintenance' (Parks Department), suggesting chronic understaffing
Potential safety hazard: branches over sidewalks and streets pose risk to pedestrians and vehicles
reporting_angles: Inspect specific locations from this week's complaints; interview Parks Department about crew availability and response times
Contact community board to ask whether they've received resident complaints about hazardous branches prior to this week

themes_detail.label: Sidewalk deterioration crisis
themes_detail.summary: Sidewalk condition complaints jumped to 12 THIS WEEK versus a 3.8 weekly average over 8 weeks—a 220% spike (z-score: 4.3)—indicating potential infrastructure failure or weather damage across the district.
evidence: 12 sidewalk condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 3.8 weekly average (220% increase, z-score: 4.3)
Compounds existing street condition complaints (724 over 90 days), suggesting systemic infrastructure stress
Community board's standing budget request for 'improve traffic and pedestrian safety' (DOT) indicates this is a persistent, unresolved concern
reporting_angles: Map this week's 12 complaints by location; visit sites to document trip hazards, heaving, or deterioration patterns
Interview DOT about maintenance backlog and whether recent weather (rain, freeze-thaw cycles) triggered the spike

themes_detail.label: Street sweeping neglect
themes_detail.summary: Street sweeping complaints surged to 4 THIS WEEK from a 0.5 weekly baseline—a 700% spike (z-score: 3.5)—paired with 220% spike in unsanitary pigeon complaints and 220% spike in residential disposal complaints, pointing to a sanitation workforce or scheduling problem.
evidence: 4 street sweeping complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly baseline (700% increase, z-score: 3.5)
3 unsanitary pigeon condition complaints last week vs. 0.4 baseline (700% increase, z-score: 5.42)—both likely linked to accumulated food waste and debris
8 residential disposal complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 2.5 baseline (220% increase, z-score: 3.48)—suggests garbage management crisis feeding pigeon problem
reporting_angles: Interview Sanitation Department about why Riverdale/Fieldston sweeping schedule changed this week; check for staffing shortage or equipment failure
Visit neighborhoods to observe debris accumulation and pigeon activity; photograph conditions for visual evidence

themes_detail.label: Vendor enforcement surge
themes_detail.summary: Vendor enforcement complaints exploded to 3 LAST WEEK from a 0.2 weekly average—a 1,100% spike (z-score: 6.35, highest severity)—suggesting either illegal street vending concentration or an enforcement crackdown, requiring immediate clarification.
evidence: 3 vendor enforcement complaints last week vs. 0.2 weekly average (1,100% increase, z-score: 6.35—highest statistical severity)
Timing and magnitude suggest either new enforcement initiative by Department of Consumer Affairs or concentrated illegal vendor activity
Lack of prior pattern makes this a highly anomalous, newsworthy event
reporting_angles: Contact Department of Consumer Affairs to ask whether enforcement operation or complaint trend began last week; request details on vendor types and locations
Interview community board members to understand whether residents complained to elected officials about vendors, triggering enforcement response

themes_detail.label: For-hire vehicle problem returning
themes_detail.summary: For-hire vehicle complaints spiked to 4 TWO WEEKS AGO versus a 0.9 weekly average—a 357% increase (z-score: 5.21)—possibly indicating Uber/Lyft congestion or parking violations in residential areas, though signal is aging.
evidence: 4 for-hire vehicle complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.9 weekly baseline (357% increase, z-score: 5.21)
Occurs within broader context of 3,293 illegal parking complaints over 90 days (second-highest complaint category)
Community board's repeated budget request for 'improve traffic and pedestrian safety' (DOT) suggests residents view this as chronic issue
reporting_angles: Determine whether the 2-week-old spike has subsided or is continuing; check latest week's data for trend direction
Interview residents in commercial corridors about for-hire vehicle double-parking and congestion patterns
